For the last report this morning I would like to provide an update on the North Kiwanis Memorial Park wash and pilot project which is part of the city's broader strategy to expand access to public washrooms and drinking water.
This pilot began in October of 2024 introducing full time supervision at the North Kiwanis washroom site during regular operating hours prior to this.
This site was only monitored through three daily commissioner checks per day.
Through December 31st 2025 with funding improved by city council earlier this year.

The goal of the additional oversight was to reduce vandalism, misuse and closures due to damage issues that have historically affected downtown washroom sites the results have been encouraging on the pilot thus far.
The reported total number of incidents have dropped by 31% between May and September compared to the previous year.
incidents requiring repairs and significant cleanup fell by 67%.
In July and August this year the site served over 63 hundred users with only one closure for additional cleaning which lasted just six and a half hours.
Historically each incident requiring repairs resulted in an average cost of $5,000.
From a cost benefit perspective if the additional oversight prevents at least 51 incidents that would typically require repairs the cost of monitoring offsets the cost of repairs.
Most incidents that have been reported involved individuals being escorted out and the presence of supervision has clearly helped determine misuse before damage occurs.
This has also reduced the burden on our facilities staff allowing them to focus on proactive maintenance and other priorities.
Financially the additional oversight costs of 50 or 254,6.
Financially the additional oversight costs of 254,600 annually is projected however no funding is currently allocated beyond the end of this year.
A business plan option has been submitted for council's consideration during the 2026-2027 budget process.
If no further direction is provided the pilot with the increased supervision will end at the end of this year and the site will return to its previous monitoring schedule of three inspections daily.
The administration will continue to explore partnerships and options to expand public washroom access in the Pleasant Hill and Riversdale areas as directed by city council.
